newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Aer Rianta wins major Hong Kong contract.
newsitem.headline: Irish Aer Rianta wins major Hong Kong contract.

text.p: State-owned Irish airport operator Aer Rianta has landed a 125 million Irish pounds a year contract to run 12 duty free shops at a major new airport in Hong Kong, Irish media said on Monday.
Aer Rianta won a contract to sell spirits and tobacco at the Hong Kong airport, Chek Lap Kok Airport, which is due to open in April 1998, reports said.

The Irish airport authority has already gained a foothold in China with a consultancy contract at duty-free shops at Beijing International Airport, and looks well positioned to become involved in a major new state-of-the-art international terminal due to open in Beijing in 1998.

Aer Rianta bid for the Hong Kong contract after entering a consortium with two international financial backers and setting up a joint venture in which it has a majority holding with Adhaven, a Belfast company and Allied Group Ltd of Hong Kong.
